title: Grade 8 Science — Tue, May 19
description: Crop Production & Management — Day 2 of 5: Sowing, irrigation, and fertilizers
subject: science

questions.question: What is sowing?
options: The process of placing seeds in prepared soil
questions.explanation: Sowing = placing seeds in the soil at proper depth and spacing for germination. Done by hand, seed drill, or broadcast.

questions.question: A seed drill is used for:
options: Sowing seeds at correct depth and spacing uniformly
questions.explanation: Seed drill sows seeds uniformly at correct depth with proper spacing — reduces seed waste and ensures better germination.

questions.question: Which seeds are suitable for sowing?
options: Clean, healthy, disease-free seeds of high quality/high-yielding variety
questions.explanation: Good seeds: high germination rate, disease-free, true to variety (certified). Poor seeds lead to poor yield.

questions.question: Irrigation means:
options: Supplying water to crops at appropriate intervals
questions.explanation: Irrigation = artificial supply of water to agricultural land. Essential where rainfall is insufficient or erratic.

questions.question: Which irrigation method is most water-efficient?
questions.explanation: Drip irrigation delivers water directly to plant roots through pipes/nozzles — minimal wastage. Most efficient method, especially for water-scarce regions.

questions.question: Sprinkler irrigation is best suited for:
options: Paddy (rice) fields that need flooded conditions
Uneven terrain and crops like wheat, vegetables, lawns
questions.explanation: Sprinkler: sprays water like rainfall — good for uneven land and crops that don't need waterlogging. Used for vegetables, wheat, coffee.

questions.question: Manure vs Fertilizer — which is organic?
options: Manure is organic (animal/plant waste); fertilizers are generally chemical/inorganic
questions.explanation: Manure: decomposed animal/plant matter — organic, improves soil texture. Fertilizers: manufactured chemicals (urea, DAP) — fast nutrients but may harm soil long-term.

questions.question: Which is an advantage of manure over chemical fertilizers?
options: Improves soil texture, water retention, and microbial life; environmentally friendly
questions.explanation: Manure improves soil structure, adds humus, promotes beneficial microorganisms, and is sustainable. Chemical fertilizers may leach, cause pollution, and degrade soil over time.

questions.question: The main nutrients needed by plants (NPK) stand for:
questions.explanation: NPK = Nitrogen (N, for leaf growth), Phosphorus (P, for roots and flowers), Potassium (K=Kalium, for overall health). Primary macronutrients for plants.

questions.question: Overuse of chemical fertilizers leads to:
options: Soil degradation, water pollution (eutrophication), loss of soil microbes, and reduced long-term fertility
questions.explanation: Chemical fertilizer overuse: nitrate leaching pollutes groundwater, eutrophication in water bodies, kills soil microbes, reduces organic matter, hard crusty soil.

questions.question: What is transplantation in agriculture?
options: Growing seedlings in nursery, then moving them to the main field when ready
questions.explanation: Transplantation: seedlings grow in a nursery bed for some weeks, then transplanted to the main field. Used for rice, tomato, cabbage.

questions.question: Green manure is:
options: Crops grown and ploughed into the soil before seeding main crop — adds nitrogen and organic matter
questions.explanation: Green manure: leguminous crops (like sunhemp, dhaincha) grown and then ploughed in — they fix nitrogen and add organic matter. Natural, sustainable fertilization.

questions.question: Waterlogging (excess water) in fields causes:
options: Better crop growth due to more water
Root rot, oxygen deficiency in soil, death of crops, and soil compaction
questions.explanation: Waterlogging: no oxygen in soil → roots cannot respire → root rot → plant death. Also promotes fungal diseases.

questions.question: Why is it important to check soil moisture before irrigation?
options: To save money on water bills
To prevent overwatering (waterlogging) and underwatering — both harm crops
Because water is free from canals
To ensure crops get no water stress at all
questions.explanation: Soil moisture checks ensure water is given when needed — avoids waterlogging (anaerobic root conditions) and drought stress (wilting, stunted growth).

questions.question: Summary: which combination of practices maximizes crop yield?
options: Proper soil preparation + quality seeds + timely irrigation + balanced fertilization (manure + chemical)
Only irrigation, no soil preparation needed
Only pest control, other practices don't matter
questions.explanation: Integrated approach: soil prep + quality seeds + right irrigation + balanced nutrition + pest control. No single factor alone ensures high yield.
